newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dow Chemical in Thai 300,000/T polyethylene plan.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical in Thai 300,000/T polyethylene plan.

text.p: The Dow Chemical Co plans to build a 300,000-tonne per year polyethylene plant in Thailand in a joint venture with Siam Cement Group, Dow said on Tuesday.
The $120 million venture is expected to come on stream in the first quarter of 1999 and will be called Siam Polyethylene Co Ltd., the company said at a news conference in Singapore.
Dow is the world's biggest producer of polyethylene and the plant will be the company's first in Asia.
President and chief executive officer William Stavropoulos said the new plant would be built at a Dow-constructed site at Map Ta Phut and Dow's share would be taken up by subsidiary Dow Plastics.
The ethylene feedstock will be provided by a 600,000-tonne per year cracker owned by Rayong Olefins Co Ltd -- a consortium company led by Siam Cement.
Siam Polyethylene will own 22 percent of Rayong Olefins.

"This investment is a strategic step for the global polyethylene business and demonstrates our strong commitment to be a key supplier to customers throughout ASEAN," he said referring to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
The plant will produce traditional polyethylenes and resins.
Stavropoulos said the technology involved will allow the plant to produce a wide range of products on the same production train, instead of setting up several trains.
ASEAN comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
